## f86321db133e

**Finding A1 — canonical demonstrations underdetermine equal-area tie-breaking.**
The intended rule extracts colored components, sorts by area descending, breaks
equal-area ties by color ascending, and packs the shapes left-to-right. The
plausible rival instead breaks equal-area ties by the components' input
reading order. That rival fits all 3/3 canonical pairs.

An ordinary generator draw (`difficulty=easy`, `seed=0`, `sample_index=5`, no
overrides) contains a size-3 color-9 component earlier in reading order and a
size-3 color-4 component later. The target exports no `self_check` hook, but the
input is an unmodified ordinary output of its documented sampler. The canonical
Racket authority (`executed_rule_hash=d8dc83bd8c28`) puts color 4 first; the
reading-order rival puts color 9 first. The first disagreement is output cell
`(row=0,col=0)`: authority `4`, rival `9`. The Racket result matches an
independent intended-rule mirror and differs from the rival.

Evidence: `checks/audit/f86321db133e/counterexample.json` is the compact,
self-contained record; `input.json`, `racket.json`, `rival.json`,
`diagnostic.json`, and `comparison.json` retain the full derivation. Generator
SHA-256: `36436ddc04bc5ae174d76cb7fec4054b9f6afd560dd8878657b0c136bba7dd87`.
No fix was attempted because this target is audit-only.
